question.:question/problem: Find where the normal line to the curve $f(x)=10 x^{2} + 5 x$ at the point $(1,15)$ intersects the $x$-axis.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x)=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(10 x^{2} + 5 x)=20 x + 5.\end{aligned}
$$

So the slope of the tangent line is

$$
m=f'(1)=25=25,
$$

and therefore the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{(25)}=- \frac{1}{25}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(15)&=- \frac{1}{25}(x-(1))\\y&=- \frac{1}{25}x-(- \frac{1}{25})+(15)\\y&=- \frac{1}{25}x+\frac{376}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we find the point of intersection with the $x$-axis by setting $y=0$ and solving the resulting equation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}- \frac{1}{25}x+\frac{376}{25}&=0\\x&=376.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal line intersects the $x$-axis at $(376,0).$

question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=18 x^{2} - 36 x + 30$ at the point $(0,30)$ intersects the $x$-axis.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Taking the derivative, we have

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(18 x^{2} - 36 x + 30)=36 x - 36.
$$

So the slope of the tangent line is

$$
m=f'(0)=-36=-36,
$$

and therefore the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{(-36)}=\frac{1}{36}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(30)&=\frac{1}{36}(x-(0))\\y&=\frac{1}{36}x+30.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we find the point of intersection with the $x$-axis by setting $y=0$ and solving the resulting equation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{36}x+30&=0\\\frac{1}{36}x&=-30\\x&=-1080.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal line intersects the $x$-axis at $(-1080,0).$

question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=\frac{20}{x}+10$ at the point $(1,30)$ intersects the $x$-axis.

The normal line intersects the $x$-axis at
$($

{{field-2}} $).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\frac{20}{x}+10)\\&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(10 + \frac{20}{x})\\&=-20x^{-2}\\&=- \frac{20}{x^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the slope of the tangent line is

$$
m=f'(1)=-20=-20,
$$

and therefore the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{(-20)}=\frac{1}{20}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(30)&=\frac{1}{20}(x-(1))\\y&=\frac{1}{20}x-(\frac{1}{20})+(30)\\y&=\frac{1}{20}x+\frac{599}{20}.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we find the point of intersection with the $x$-axis by setting $y=0$ and solving the resulting equation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{20}x+\frac{599}{20}&=0\\x&=-599.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal line intersects the  $x$-axis at $(-599,0).$
